guard: running a mapped command against a real broker and manager compares the endpoint requests it issued with the owner rows, so a row naming another command fails
why: The execution half is what catches a wrong owner the offline grammar accepts; removing its comparison must redden the self-test that feeds it one.

mutations.name: an issued command is no longer compared with its owner
mutations.find: if (!ownedByRun(item)) problems.push(`cotal ${label} issued ${req.endpoint} ${req.command}, whose owner is ${map.owners[item] ?? "missing"}`);
mutations.expectRed: a row that names another command for manager ps fails on the same observation
mutations.cell: a row that names another command for manager ps fails on the same observation
